analysis.investment_thesis: Campus Activewear holds a meaningful brand position in India's mass-market athleisure footwear segment with strong ROE (29.5%) and improving free cash flow, but revenue growth has stalled — FY24 actually declined 2.4% and FY25 recovered only ~10% — which at a 55x P/E leaves little margin for error. Fisher's growth premium is not warranted when the compounding engine has visibly slowed.
key_strengths: Strong capital efficiency: ROE 29.5% and ROCE 31.8% indicate the business earns well above its cost of capital
FCF turning meaningfully positive: INR 219 Cr in FY24 and 176 Cr in FY25 after years of near-zero free cash flow
Large underpenetrated TAM: India's branded sports footwear market is still in early innings, giving long runway if growth reignites
key_risks: Growth deceleration is alarming — revenue fell in FY24, recovered only ~10% in FY25; net profit essentially flat at INR 117→89→121 Cr over three years
Operating margin compression from ~20% in FY22 to ~11.5% in FY25 signals pricing pressure and/or cost structure deterioration — the opposite of what Fisher wants to see

No visible R&D or product innovation pipeline; CAMPUS competes on price against entrenched domestic players (Relaxo, Action, Bata) and aspirational international brands (Nike, Adidas), with no clear moat
red_flags: Revenue declined in FY24 (-2.4%) — a Fisher disqualifier: he wants consistent 20%+ growth, not contraction
Operating margin halved from FY22 peak (20.3%) to current ~11.5% — eroding the quality of earnings
P/E of 55.7x ascribes exceptional growth expectations to a business that is currently growing single digits in revenue and flat in profits
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From the scuttlebutt perspective, Campus tells a familiar story of a mid-market Indian consumer brand that rode post-COVID athleisure tailwinds to rapid growth (FY22: +68% revenue, FY23: +24%), then ran into the wall of demand normalization. The FY24 revenue dip to INR 1,448 Cr from INR 1,484 Cr and the dramatic operating profit collapse from INR 242 Cr (FY22) to INR 143 Cr (FY24) expose a business lacking genuine pricing power. Fisher demands evidence that a company is actively investing in products that will sustain growth for 10+ years — I see no R&D line item, no technology edge, and the brand lives in the value segment where consumers are highly price-sensitive.

The financial structure has improved — D/E is a manageable 0.48, OCF has been positive all five years, and the balance sheet is strengthening (equity up to INR 757 Cr). These are real positives. But at 55x trailing earnings with profits growing from INR 117 Cr to INR 121 Cr over two years, the market is paying a growth price for a business delivering value-stock earnings growth. Fisher would hold existing positions given the brand's long-term potential in India's consumption story, but would absolutely not add at this valuation until management demonstrates a credible path back to 20%+ revenue growth with margin recovery.
